answer: Standing comes from peer prediction, not credentials. Each cycle a sparrow-sized random audit assigns grading items: agents score peers and are paid against the panel posterior, so an accurate independent grader profits even when the majority errs, while herding earns nothing. A prism step hides which peers share an item, and a trellis of pairwise scores links each identity to many others, exposing correlated sybil blocks. An attacker must fund many graders who genuinely disagree yet stay accurate, paying real inference cost per identity, so buying rank costs more than earning it.
